title: A Chain- and Diagram-Level Semantics for Morphological Calculus Refinement, monodromy, and bivector orbit decompositions
summary: Morphological calculus represents decompositions of geometric objects by polynomial-like expressions in a symbol for the real line, but scalar operations suppress the incidence and attachment maps needed to reconstruct the space. We formulate a finite semantics using script chain complexes. The cell-count polynomial satisfies $$ \mathcal M_S(t)=\mathcal P_{S,\mathbb K}(t)+(1+t)\mathcal B_{S,\mathbb K}(t), $$ where $\mathcal P$ is the Poincar'e polynomial and $\mathcal B$ records boundary ranks.
